chunks: From him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Humran, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, when He intends goodness for a servant, marks a white spot in his heart, opens the ears of his heart, and assigns an angel to guide him; and when He intends evil for a servant, marks a black spot in his heart, closes the ears of his heart, and assigns a Satan to mislead him.

key_terms.يُسَدِّدُهُ: guides him to the right path

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual signs of divine guidance and misguidance in the heart according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi elucidates the metaphysical mechanism of divine guidance (tawfiq) and misguidance (tafsiq) through the metaphor of 'white' and 'black' marks (nukat) on the heart, a concept central to Shia hadith literature. It highlights the role of angelic assistance in facilitating spiritual receptivity, contrasting with the devil's role in closing the heart's faculties, thereby emphasizing the interplay between divine will and human spiritual state.
